payload.choice: LEAP-1: a 1/16-scale 4WD cab-over truck (Optimus silhouette) that is a race car, a ramp jumper, and a standing robot in one toy
payload.why: One machine, three tricks. 1/16 scale (~35 cm, under 900 g) is the sweet spot: light enough to survive jump landings, big enough to hold a transform mechanism, safe for a 6-year-old's hands.

payload.choice: Brushed 390 motor, 4WD shaft drive, 2S LiFe battery, ~20 km/h top speed, with a parent-set 50% training mode in the ESC
payload.why: Feels genuinely fast at kid height but stays steerable. 4WD keeps it tracking straight on jump run-ups and landings. Training mode means the same car grows with the driver.

payload.choice: Jumps come from ramps, not actuators: 35 mm travel oil-damped coilovers on double wishbones, 40 mm ground clearance, belly skid plate, foam-filled rubber tires, slight nose-heavy balance (55/45)
payload.why: Physics-honest: an onboard jump actuator would add weight and break. The suspension's whole job is the landing; nose-heavy balance makes it land flat instead of looping onto its tail.

payload.choice: Three servo-driven stages, a simplified Robosen: (1) rear chassis folds down at a mid hinge to become legs, rear wheels become heels; (2) front wheel pods swing out to become arms; (3) head pops up from behind the cab. Five metal-gear micro servos with mechanical hard stops
payload.why: Each stage is one rotation of one hinge, so a kid can watch and understand the mechanism. Hard stops mean the plastic, not the servo gears, defines the end pose.

payload.choice: In car mode every folding joint locks into an over-center latch, and firmware only allows transforming when the IMU says the car is still and level
payload.why: Jumping and transforming fight each other: landings hammer exactly the joints the transform needs to be free. The latch routes landing forces through solid plastic and steel pins, never servo teeth; the interlock stops a mid-air transform button-mash from stripping gears.

payload.choice: The robot poses, turns at the waist, lights up its chest, and scoots on small wheels hidden in its feet — it does not walk
payload.why: Walking is a far harder, more fragile machine. Skating on hidden foot wheels keeps robot mode drivable with the same radio, so the toy stays fun in both shapes.

payload.choice: Standard 4-channel 2.4 GHz radio; channel 3 button triggers a transform choreography on a small microcontroller (RP2040) with an IMU for the still-and-level interlock and an auto-recover fold-back if it tips over
payload.why: The radio stays ordinary and replaceable; all cleverness lives in one cheap board. Auto-recover means a crashed robot folds itself back to car mode instead of ending the play session.

payload.choice: No finger-pinch gaps under 12 mm on folding joints, rounded bumpers, battery behind a parent-only screw latch, LiFe chemistry, training-mode throttle
payload.why: Designed for a 6-year-old co-pilot: LiFe tolerates crashes far better than LiPo, and the pinch rule is checked on every hinge in the CAD before printing.

payload.choice: Three weekends: (1) cheap 1/16 4WD donor chassis driving fast, (2) build ramps and tune suspension for jumps, (3) bolt on the 3D-printed transform module (PETG)
payload.why: Each stage is a complete toy on its own, so the project never stalls waiting for the hard part. The transform module bolts to the chassis plate and can be rebuilt after breakage.

payload.choice: Deliverable: a self-contained three.js page with three acts — sprint, ramp jump, transform — in Optimus red/blue, geometry kept to boxes and cylinders so the mechanism reads clearly
payload.why: The animation is the shared drawing board: father and son can watch the hinge order before anything is printed, and the same stage order becomes the servo choreography.

payload.choice: leap1.html shipped: self-contained three.js animation of the sprint, ramp jump, and three-stage transform, committed beside this account
payload.why: Verified frame by frame in a headless browser: car mode, air time, landing, mid-fold, robot mode, wave, and the victory lap all render correctly
